Person who travels regularly between home and work — Persona que viaja a diario al trabajo / viajero habitual.
The train was full of commuters.
Verb: commute. Noun: the commute, meaning the daily journey.
Keep someone or something in a small space — Confinar / encerrar.
The dog was confined to the kitchen.
Please confine your answer to one page.
v|Noun: confinement. Pattern: confine to or confine within.
Not working or being used — Parado/a / inactivo/a.
The machines stood idle all week.
He is an idle young man.
v|Careful: idle is lazy, idol is someone admired.
Person or thing loved and admired greatly — ídolo.
The singer is a teenage idol.
An image worshipped as a god — ídolo.
They prayed before a stone idol.
Do not jest about serious matters.
v|Phrase: in jest, meaning not seriously.
Showing love for your country — Patriótico/a.
Noun: patriotism. A person is a patriot.
Great bravery, especially in battle — Valor / valentía.
He received a medal for valor.
Extremely foolish or wildly behaved person — Loco/a / insensato/a.
Old word for mentally ill; avoid it for real illness.
Tube that carries blood back to the heart — Vena.
The nurse found a vein in his arm.
A line of mineral in rock — Veta / filón.
They found a vein of silver.
A mood or style — Tono / estilo.
He continued in a humorous vein.
Careful: a vein carries blood to the heart, an artery carries it away.
With nothing exciting happening — Sin incidentes / tranquilo/a.
Often a good thing: an uneventful flight.
Able to produce good crops — Fértil.
Mention or speak about — Referirse a.
He referred to the accident only once.
Send someone to another person for help — Remitir / derivar.
The doctor referred me to a specialist.
Look at something for information — Consultar.
Great pain, worry or sorrow — Angustia / aflicción.
The news caused her great distress.
The ship sent out a distress signal.
Make someone very unhappy — Angustiar / afligir.
It distressed me to see him cry.
Make or become smaller or less — Disminuir / aminorar.
Drive at the maximum speed allowed.
Opposite: minimum. Plural: maximums or maxima.
Old people are vulnerable to the cold.
Noun: vulnerability. Pattern: vulnerable to something.
Mean; be a sign of — Significar.
Show what you think by a sign — Manifestar / indicar.
Signify your agreement by raising a hand.
The old stories of a people about gods and heroes — Mitología.
Greek mythology is full of monsters.
Adjective: mythological. A single story is a myth.
Someone you work with — Colega / compañero/a de trabajo.
Careful: in English colleague is for work, not for a school friend.
v|The verb is stressed last, the noun first.
Supply something that is needed — Proporcionar / suministrar.
State as a condition in a rule — Estipular / disponer.
The contract provides that payment is monthly.
v|Patterns: provide something for someone, provide someone with something.
Being faithful to a person, group or idea — Lealtad / fidelidad.
His loyalty to the team never changed.
Person who offers to work without being paid or forced — Voluntario/a.
Offer to do something freely — Ofrecerse / presentarse voluntario.
An unfair opinion formed without knowing the facts — Prejuicio.
He has a prejudice against foreigners.
High and sharp in sound — Estridente / chillón.
A shrill whistle stopped the game.
Cheerful and full of fun — Alegre / jovial.
Comparative: jollier. British English also uses jolly for very: jolly good.
Clever and amusing in what you say — Ingenioso/a / ocurrente.
Make something harder to do — Dificultar / entorpecer.
Treat someone badly or cruelly — Maltratar / abusar de.
He was accused of abusing his staff.
Use something wrongly — Abusar de / hacer mal uso de.
Cruel or wrong treatment, noun — Maltrato / abuso.
The report describes years of abuse.
v|The noun ends in a soft s sound, the verb in a z sound.
Speak quietly and unclearly — Mascullar / murmurar.
Turn the sound off — Silenciar / quitar el sonido.
v|Also a mute letter, like the b in doubt.
Keep something; continue to have — Retener / conservar.
Keep something in your memory — Retener / recordar.
Person who applies for a job or stands for election — Candidato/a.
Three candidates applied for the post.
Come or go before — Preceder / anteceder.
A short film preceded the main feature.
v|Noun: the preceding chapter. Careful: precede is to go before, proceed is to go on.
Young person between child and adult — Adolescente.
Of or like a teenager — Adolescente.
Teaching boys and girls together — Mixto/a / coeducativo/a.
Person with extreme political views — Radical.
He was a radical in his youth.
Adverb: radically. From the Latin for root.
The crowd gave a spontaneous cheer.
Take something off the surface — Desnatar / espumar.
Skim the fat off the soup.
Read something quickly — Leer por encima / echar un vistazo.
Move lightly over a surface — Rozar / pasar rozando.
Give someone a vaccine against a disease — Vacunar.
Not neat; in disorder — Desordenado/a / descuidado/a.
A tool or container used in the house — Utensilio.
Knives and spoons are kitchen utensils.
Easily hurt or offended — Sensible / susceptible.
He is sensitive about his height.
Quick to feel small changes — Sensible.
This is a very sensitive microphone.
Noun: sensitivity. False friend: sensible in English means reasonable.
Neither very hot nor very cold — Templado/a.
